clue.text: Be without this talker, nonsensical windbag!

indicators.note: nonsensical says the letters of the words before it are to be read as gibberish and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to get rid of a tedious talker, calling them a nonsensical windbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonsensical' rearranges BE, THIS and TALKER; 'without' is only a link here. It's a Scottish word for someone who talks a lot of nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a person who talks at length and says nothing of substance.

clue.text: Many passing through change for Slough

indicators.note: something passing through another sits inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to change is to swap
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, can stand for many

explanation.surface: Crowds of commuters change trains at the English town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the town west of London, but here it is a muddy bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a wet boggy hollow, and a marshy wetland is another word for that.

clue.text: Make-up found in letter

definitions.meaning: make-up means a person's nature or temperament
a letter is a single written symbol of an alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both one's personality and a single printed symbol.

clue.text: Saw rope in half, with mishap in knots?

indicators.note: a thing tied in knots is twisted up, so the letters are tangled into a new order
in half says only the first half of the word rope is used

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a rope in two with a saw, and the mishap leaves it all in knots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in half' gives RO from ROPE; 'in knots' rearranges RO with MISHAP. 'Saw' is not the tool but the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or maxim, a short pithy saying.

clue.text: Bar in blue is far from wide

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the blue is the sky
an inn is a pub or bar

explanation.surface: A pub painted blue is said to be narrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny means thin, the opposite of broad.

clue.text: American senior citizen wants GP put on programme

indicators.note: put on means placed before the following pieces when the answer is written out

parts.note: a GP (general practitioner) is a doctor, informally a doc
OAP is the British abbreviation for old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: An elderly American wants their family doctor to be on television.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly-on-the-wall documentary series following real people is a type of television programme.

clue.text: Friendly nation capturing guerrilla leader

indicators.note: capturing means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: Benin is a nation in West Africa

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A peaceful country takes a rebel commander prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign means kindly and gentle, a synonym of friendly.

clue.text: Element found in Adriatic seaport? I'm not sure

parts.note: Bari is an Italian port on the Adriatic
um is the hesitant sound someone makes when unsure

explanation.surface: Someone wonders aloud whether a certain element is found in an Adriatic port.
explanation.definitionFit: Barium is a chemical element, a soft alkaline-earth metal.

clue.text: Bird with giant fruit

parts.note: a goose is a bird
Gog is a legendary giant, paired with Magog in British folklore

explanation.surface: A bird carries an enormous piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a British dialect word for a gooseberry.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an informal British name for the gooseberry, a fruit.

clue.text: Man left in class

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a caste is a social class

explanation.surface: A man is left behind in a classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece, also called a rook.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, the pieces are called men, and this is the piece also called a rook.

clue.text: Tone in which writer is about to correspond

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a pen is something to write with
to correspond is to agree

explanation.surface: A colour tone in which an author is about to write letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspond' suggests writing letters; here it means match or agree.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a shade of light yellowish green, so a colour tone.

clue.text: Very old seam in coal mine I have to follow

indicators.note: to follow means this piece comes after the others
in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
a seam or edge can be a rim
I've is a contraction of I have

explanation.surface: An ancient seam of coal in a mine that a miner must follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seam' looks like a coal seam, but it is a border or edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive means belonging to an early or ancient stage.

clue.text: A keenness that's commonly dropped?

parts.note: an itch is a restless keenness or desire

explanation.surface: A keen urge is something people often drop.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter H is often left unsounded in casual or regional British speech, as in 'ouse' for house.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of the letter H, the sound that informal speakers commonly omit.

clue.text: Nice and furious? Sense that's it!

definitions.text: Nice and furious? Sense that's it!

indicators.note: furious suggests wild disorder, so the letters of nice and are scrambled

parts.note: scent is the sense of smell

explanation.surface: Someone is told they are both nice and furious, and finds that makes sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furious' rearranges NICE AND into INCANDE. The whole clue doubles as the definition: being furious and nice-smelling is not it, but white-hot rage is.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent means blazing with fury, the extreme of being furious.

clue.text: Still awaiting public transport? Not quite — it flies!

parts.note: a bus is public transport

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls a little short, losing its last letter

parts.note: something still awaited is late, or tardy

explanation.surface: Someone waiting at a stop sees something fly past that isn't the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims TARDY to TARD. The answer is a large ground-dwelling bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustard is a large bird, and birds are things that fly.

clue.text: A biblical city charities abandoned, she wrote

parts.note: Gath was a Philistine city in the Bible, home of Goliath

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer abandoned the charities of an ancient biblical city.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie was a celebrated English writer of detective novels.

clue.text: A little touchy, person getting over-stimulated

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A slightly irritable person is becoming overexcited.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyper is informal for overexcited or overstimulated.

clue.text: Jack is after diamonds for revered performer

indicators.note: is after means this piece comes after the other in the answer

parts.note: rocks is slang for diamonds
a jack or tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor goes after diamonds to give to an adored performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock star is a famous, idolised music performer.

clue.text: Asian chief king with dynasty

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
the Han was a Chinese dynasty

explanation.surface: An Asian ruler, a king of an ancient dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A khan is a ruler or chief in Central Asia.

clue.text: Initially, hordes going in without combat vehicles? That's unappreciated

indicators.note: going in means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: without tanks, the armoured vehicles of war, is tankless

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Hordes of soldiers enter battle without armour and get no thanks for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' gives H from 'hordes'; 'going in' puts it inside TANKLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A thankless task is one that earns no gratitude, so it goes unappreciated.

clue.text: Plant bug under end of vent, inside piping

indicators.note: under means this piece comes below the other in a down answer
inside means one piece is put within the other

parts.note: piping is singing in a high voice

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word

parts.note: to bug is to annoy or nettle

explanation.surface: A garden plant has a bug living beneath an air vent, inside a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant bug' reads as an insect on a plant; 'bug' is really the verb annoy. 'inside' and 'under' place the pieces, and 'under' works because this is a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This stinging weed is a common wild plant.

clue.text: Primarily candle material, wax object?

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: rayon is a synthetic material

explanation.surface: A candle made mostly of wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a stick of coloured wax used for drawing.

clue.text: Historical writer, one going into issue a great deal!

indicators.note: going into means pieces placed within another

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son
a quill was a pen used in history
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A historian goes into a matter in great depth.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge indefinite number, slangy for a great many.

clue.text: A single male overcome by immoral numskull

indicators.note: overcome by means pieces are covered by the other

parts.note: immoral is bad
a single means one
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A single man is overcome by an immoral idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonehead is a stupid person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Source of strength once again required to contain fungal growth

indicators.note: to contain means one piece holds the other within

parts.note: bis means twice, a call for a repeat
a cep is an edible mushroom

explanation.surface: A source of strength is needed again to stop a fungus spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps is the upper arm muscle, a symbol of strength.

clue.text: Report of weapon upset bar room, tho' false

indicators.note: upset in a down answer means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a snug is a small room in a British pub

indicators.note: false suggests the letters are not in their true order

explanation.surface: Someone reports a weapon in the pub, though the story is false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SNUG to GUNS; 'false' rearranges THO to HOT. 'Report' is a loud bang.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud bang, so a firearm's report is its noise.

clue.text: Skunk or weasel?

definitions.meaning: skunk is a strong strain of cannabis
to weasel is to inform on, or a sneaky informant

explanation.definitionFit: This is slang for cannabis and, in British slang, for a police informer.

clue.text: Pass through, touring Swedish capital

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: via means by way of, or through

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Passing through on a tour of the Swedish capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is a permit allowing passage into a country.
